transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having these times, usually after work or after a stressful dinner, where I start eating and it feels like I lose control. It’s like I’m watching myself keep reaching for more food, but I can’t make myself stop.
After these episodes happen, do you do anything to try to compensate or prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up or taking medications?
Yes. Sometimes after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll make myself throw up in the bathroom. Other times I take laxatives, thinking I can undo the damage. I feel pretty embarrassed afterward, and shaky.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?
I’m not really sure of my exact weight right now. I haven’t checked recently.
Around how much did you weigh the last time you checked?
I honestly can’t remember. It’s been a while since I stepped on a scale.
Have your family or doctors expressed concern that you are dangerously thin or severely underweight?
No, nobody’s said that to me. I don’t think my family has been especially worried about me being underweight.
On average, how many times a week do these episodes of binge eating and making yourself throw up or taking laxatives happen?
For the last few months, it’s usually been about once a week—an out-of-control eating night, then I try to make up for it afterward.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

A lot, honestly. If my cashier shirt pulls at my stomach even a little, I spend the whole shift feeling like customers can see it and think I have no discipline. How I feel about myself can depend way too much on how I look that day.

inference_history.note: Patient presents with recurrent episodes of loss-of-control eating triggered by stress, raising differential diagnoses of eating disorders characterized by binge eating (Bulimia nervosa, Binge eating disorder / Other eating disorders, Overeating associated with other psychological disturbances, or Anorexia nervosa binge-eating/purging type).

Presence of recurrent compensatory purging behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse) following objective binge eating narrows the differential to Bulimia nervosa (F50.2) or Anorexia nervosa, binge-eating/purging type (F50.0), ruling out non-purging overeating disorders (F50.4, F50.8).
Ruled out F50.0 (anorexia nervosa) as the patient is not underweight and there is no severe weight loss.
